topic: Absence of Deed: Interest on Partner's Loan
questionText:
A firm is dissolved compulsorily in the following cases:
(A) When all the partners or all but one partner, become insolvent,
rendering them incompetent to sign a contract;
(B) When the business of the firm becomes illegal
(C) Change in existing profit sharing ratio among partners
(D) When some event has taken place which makes it unlawful for the
partners to carry on the business of the firm in partnership.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Erroneously assumed both statements were valid.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Rejected valid scientific statements erroneously.

options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Failed to recognize the fallacy in Statement II.

options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Statement I is false while Statement II is factually sound.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
1. (A) Insolvency of all or all but one partner: Section 41(a) compulsory ground.
2. (B) Business becomes illegal: Section 41(b) compulsory ground.
3. (C) Change in existing profit sharing ratio: Reconstitution of partnership, firm continues.
4. (D) Unlawful for partners to carry on the business: Section 41(b) compulsory ground.
5. Therefore, compulsory dissolution takes place in (A), (B), and (D) only.
Hence, option (D) is correct.

topic: Admission of Partner: Hidden Goodwill
questionText:
Which combination of statements is true about dissolution-
(A). Dissolution of a partnership is different from dissolution of a firm. 
(B). A partnership is dissolved when there is a death of a partner. 
(C). A firm is dissolved when all partners give consent to it.
 (D). A firm is compulsorily dissolved when a partner decides to retire.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Erroneously assumed both statements were valid.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Rejected valid scientific statements erroneously.

options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Statement I is true while Statement II contains a factual error.

options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Failed to recognize the fallacy in Statement I.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
1. Statement (A): Dissolution of partnership differs from dissolution of firm. True.
2. Statement (B): Partnership dissolves on death of a partner. True.
3. Statement (C): Firm dissolves by consent of all partners (Section 40). True.
4. Statement (D): 'Firm is compulsorily dissolved when a partner decides to retire.' False; continuing partners continue the firm.
5. Therefore, statements (A), (B), and (C) only are true.
Hence, option (C) is correct.

4. Step 4 (C): Calculate goodwill by multiplying super profit by number of years' purchase.
5. Sequence: (A), (B), (D), (C).
